Maintain the distinction between a motorist sharing the road and the excluded motorcycle/CDL operator curricula. The three-foot bicycle passing rule and bicycle helmet summary remain subject to current issuer/legal review. Avoid treating mirror visibility as a universal optical guarantee or changing lanes for a merging truck without checking safety. National cyclist totals, dated crash figures, truck-fatality proportions and the exact loaded-truck stopping example are not independently verified current facts. Image-only no-zone geometry remains a dedicated-surface gap. [A01] [A02] [A03] [A04] [A05] [A06]
Memory cue, authored product policy: “See and be seen; space to stop, space to turn”. The cue retrieves complete cited rules and does not replace their conditions.
Terminology: A no-zone is a truck blind area. A squeeze hazard is the space beside a wide-turning truck or bus that closes as it turns toward the curb.
Misconception to correct: A narrow motorcycle needs only part of a lane, or an empty gap ahead of a truck is unused space. The guide reserves a full lane for motorcycles and stopping room for trucks.
